partA.text: The centroid of a triangle lies at a distance from the base equal to:
partA.explanation: The centroid of a triangle is located at 1/3 the height from the base (2/3 from the apex).

partA.text: A force couple produces:
options: Pure rotation (moment) with no net force
partA.explanation: A couple consists of two equal, opposite, parallel forces producing a pure moment with zero net force.

partA.text: The coefficient of static friction is generally:
options: Equal to the coefficient of kinetic friction
Greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction
Less than the coefficient of kinetic friction
partA.explanation: Static friction coefficient is typically greater than kinetic friction coefficient for the same surfaces.

partA.text: The moment of inertia of a circular section about its centroidal axis is:
partA.explanation: For a circular cross-section, I = πd⁴/64 about the centroidal (diametral) axis.

partA.text: According to the principle of virtual work, a system is in equilibrium if the virtual work done by all forces is:
partA.explanation: Principle of virtual work: total virtual work done by all forces for a virtual displacement is zero at equilibrium.

partA.text: Newton's second law of motion states that force is directly proportional to:
partA.explanation: Newton's second law: F = dp/dt, force equals the rate of change of momentum (= ma for constant mass).

partA.text: The center of gravity of a uniform solid hemisphere of radius R lies at a distance from the flat face equal to:
partA.explanation: The centroid of a solid hemisphere lies at 3R/8 from the flat (base) face.

partA.text: Work done by a force is defined as the product of force and:
options: Displacement in the direction of the force
partA.explanation: Work = Force × displacement in the direction of the applied force.

partA.text: The radius of gyration of a body about an axis is defined such that its moment of inertia equals:
options: Mass times square of radius of gyration
Mass divided by radius of gyration
partA.explanation: I = m·k², where k is the radius of gyration.

partA.text: Hooke's law states that stress is proportional to strain within the:
partA.explanation: Hooke's Law: stress ∝ strain holds true only within the elastic limit of the material.

partA.text: The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is called:
partA.explanation: Poisson's ratio μ = lateral strain / longitudinal strain.

partA.text: The maximum shear stress theory of failure is also known as:
partA.explanation: Maximum shear stress theory is also called Tresca's theory of failure.

partA.text: For a simply supported beam with a central point load W and span L, the maximum bending moment is:
partA.explanation: Maximum bending moment for a central point load on a simply supported beam = WL/4.

partA.text: The bending equation M/I = σ/y = E/R relates bending moment to:
options: Stress, section, and radius of curvature
partA.explanation: The bending equation links bending moment M, moment of inertia I, bending stress σ, distance y, Young's modulus E, and radius of curvature R.

partA.text: A shaft subjected to pure torsion experiences maximum shear stress at:
partA.explanation: In torsion, shear stress varies linearly from zero at the center to a maximum at the outer surface.

partA.text: Euler's formula for buckling load of a column is valid for:
partA.explanation: Euler's buckling formula applies specifically to long, slender columns where buckling governs failure, not crushing.

partA.text: The strain energy stored in a body due to gradually applied load is given by:
partA.explanation: For a gradually applied load, strain energy U = ½ × P × δ (area under the load-deflection curve).

partA.text: The modulus of rigidity relates shear stress to:
partA.explanation: Modulus of rigidity (G) = shear stress / shear strain.

partA.text: The degree of freedom of a planar mechanism is calculated using:
partA.explanation: Grubler's equation (or Kutzbach criterion) determines the degrees of freedom of a planar mechanism.

partA.text: In a four-bar mechanism, if the sum of the shortest and longest link lengths is less than the sum of the other two, it is called:
partA.explanation: This is Grashof's law: if Lshortest + Llongest < Lother1 + Lother2, at least one link can fully rotate — a Grashof mechanism.

partA.text: The primary function of a flywheel in machinery is to:
options: Increase the speed of the machine
Store kinetic energy and reduce speed fluctuations
Convert rotary motion to linear motion
partA.explanation: A flywheel stores kinetic energy during high-torque phases and releases it during low-torque phases, smoothing speed fluctuations.

partA.text: Coriolis component of acceleration exists when a point has:
options: Sliding motion on a rotating link
partA.explanation: The Coriolis component arises when a point slides along a link that is itself rotating.

partA.text: The condition for a cam-follower to maintain contact at high speeds is governed by the:
partA.explanation: At high speeds, the spring (or retaining force) must be strong enough to overcome the follower's inertia to maintain contact with the cam.

partA.text: The velocity ratio of a simple gear train is the ratio of:
options: Number of teeth on driven gear to driver gear
Diameter of driver to driven gear only
Speed of driver to speed of driven gear
partA.explanation: Velocity ratio = speed of driver / speed of driven gear = teeth on driven/teeth on driver (inversely related to teeth count).

partA.text: Gyroscopic couple acts on a rotating body when there is a change in the direction of its:
partA.explanation: Gyroscopic couple arises due to the rate of change of the direction of the angular momentum (spin axis).

partA.text: The purpose of a governor in an engine is to:
options: Regulate mean speed by controlling fuel supply as load varies
partA.explanation: A governor regulates the mean speed of an engine by adjusting fuel/steam supply in response to changing load.

partA.text: The static balancing of rotating masses requires that the resultant of all centrifugal forces be:
options: Equal to the weight of the rotor
partA.explanation: For static balance, the vector sum of all centrifugal forces acting on the rotating masses must equal zero.

partA.text: The factor of safety is defined as the ratio of:
partA.explanation: Factor of safety = Ultimate (or yield) stress / permissible (working) stress.

partA.text: Fatigue failure in machine components typically occurs due to:
options: Repeated cyclic loading below the ultimate strength
partA.explanation: Fatigue failure results from repeated/cyclic stresses over time, even when stresses are well below the material's ultimate strength.

partA.text: A key used to connect a shaft and hub primarily transmits:
partA.explanation: A key transmits torque between the shaft and the hub of a gear/pulley mounted on it.

partA.text: Which type of screw thread is preferred for power transmission due to lower friction?
partA.explanation: Square threads have a lower friction angle, making them efficient for power screws.

partA.text: The endurance limit of a material refers to the stress below which:
options: The material can withstand infinite load cycles without fatigue failure
partA.explanation: Endurance (fatigue) limit is the stress amplitude below which a material can theoretically endure infinite cycles without failing.

partA.text: Preferred numbers are used in machine design mainly to:
options: Standardize dimensions in a rational series
partA.explanation: Preferred numbers form standardized geometric series used to rationalize sizes/capacities in design.

partA.text: A stress concentration factor accounts for the effect of:
options: Geometric discontinuities like holes, fillets, and notches
partA.explanation: Stress concentration factor quantifies the increase in local stress near geometric discontinuities such as holes or notches.

partA.text: Bolted joints subjected to eccentric loading experience:
options: Direct shear plus additional tensile/compressive stress due to the moment
partA.explanation: Eccentric loads create a moment causing unequal stress distribution — direct shear plus tension/compression from the induced moment.

partA.text: The primary purpose of a shaft coupling is to:
options: Connect two shafts to transmit torque/motion
partA.explanation: A coupling connects two shafts end-to-end for transmitting torque and rotational motion.

partA.text: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is:
options: Transmitted only in the direction of application
partA.explanation: Pascal's law: pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions.

partA.text: The continuity equation in fluid mechanics is based on the principle of conservation of:
partA.explanation: The continuity equation (A1V1 = A2V2 for incompressible flow) expresses conservation of mass.

partA.text: Bernoulli's equation is derived by applying the principle of conservation of:
partA.explanation: Bernoulli's equation expresses conservation of mechanical energy along a streamline for ideal, incompressible flow.

partA.text: Reynolds number is used to determine whether flow is:
partA.explanation: Reynolds number (ratio of inertial to viscous forces) distinguishes laminar flow from turbulent flow.

partA.text: The unit of dynamic viscosity in SI is:
partA.explanation: Dynamic viscosity has SI units of Pascal-seconds (Pa·s), equivalent to kg/(m·s).

partA.text: A manometer is used to measure:
partA.explanation: A manometer measures pressure (or pressure difference) using a column of liquid.

partA.text: The center of pressure on a submerged plane surface is always:
partA.explanation: The center of pressure lies below the centroid of a submerged surface due to increasing pressure with depth.

partA.text: For an incompressible fluid flowing through a pipe of varying cross-section, as the area decreases, the velocity:
partA.explanation: By continuity equation (A×V = constant), a decrease in area causes an increase in velocity.

partA.text: Cavitation in pumps occurs due to:
options: Local pressure falling below vapor pressure of the liquid
partA.explanation: Cavitation occurs when local pressure drops below the liquid's vapor pressure, forming and collapsing vapor bubbles.

partA.text: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of conservation of:
partA.explanation: First law of thermodynamics: energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted between forms (ΔU = Q - W).

partA.text: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between temperatures T1 (source) and T2 (sink) is:
partA.explanation: Carnot efficiency η = 1 - T2/T1, with temperatures in absolute (Kelvin) scale.

partA.text: According to the second law of thermodynamics, entropy of an isolated system:
partA.explanation: Second law: entropy of an isolated system never decreases; it increases for irreversible processes or stays constant for reversible ones.

partA.text: An isothermal process occurs at constant:
partA.explanation: An isothermal process is defined as occurring at constant temperature.

partA.text: An adiabatic process is one in which there is no:
options: Heat transfer to or from the system
partA.explanation: In an adiabatic process, Q = 0 — no heat is transferred into or out of the system.

partA.text: The specific heat at constant pressure (Cp) is always ______ specific heat at constant volume (Cv) for an ideal gas.
partA.explanation: For an ideal gas, Cp > Cv because at constant pressure, additional energy goes into doing work as the gas expands (Cp - Cv = R).

partA.text: The Otto cycle is the ideal air-standard cycle for:
partA.explanation: The Otto cycle models the ideal spark-ignition (petrol) engine with constant-volume heat addition.

partA.text: In a Rankine cycle, the working fluid is typically:
partA.explanation: The Rankine cycle is the ideal cycle for steam power plants, using water/steam as the working fluid.

partA.text: The Clausius statement of the second law relates to the impossibility of:
options: Heat spontaneously flowing from a colder to a hotter body without external work
partA.explanation: Clausius statement: heat cannot flow spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body without external work input.

partA.text: Fourier's law of heat conduction states that heat flux is proportional to:
partA.explanation: Fourier's law: q = -k(dT/dx), heat flux is proportional to the negative temperature gradient.

partA.text: The thermal conductivity of a material generally has SI units of:
partA.explanation: Thermal conductivity k has SI units of watts per meter-kelvin (W/m·K).

partA.text: Convective heat transfer coefficient depends on:
options: Fluid properties, flow velocity, and surface geometry
partA.explanation: Convective heat transfer coefficient (h) depends on fluid properties, flow conditions, and the geometry involved.

partA.text: Radiative heat transfer between two black bodies depends on the difference of:
options: The fourth power of their absolute temperatures
partA.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann law: radiative heat transfer ∝ (T1⁴ - T2⁴), the difference of fourth powers of absolute temperature.

partA.text: A fin is used to enhance heat transfer primarily by:
options: Increasing the surface area for convection
Increasing thermal conductivity of the base material
partA.explanation: Fins extend surface area exposed to the fluid, enhancing convective heat dissipation.

partA.text: The Nusselt number in convective heat transfer represents the ratio of:
partA.explanation: Nusselt number Nu = hL/k represents the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer across a fluid layer.

partA.text: Heat exchangers where fluids flow in opposite directions are called:
partA.explanation: In counter-flow heat exchangers, the two fluids flow in opposite directions, generally giving higher effectiveness than parallel flow.

partA.text: The Log Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD) is used in the design of:
partA.explanation: LMTD is used to calculate the effective temperature driving force for heat transfer in heat exchangers.

partA.text: Black body radiation intensity as a function of wavelength is described by:
partA.explanation: Planck's law describes the spectral distribution of black body radiation as a function of wavelength and temperature.

partA.text: In a lathe machine, the operation of reducing the diameter of a workpiece is called:
partA.explanation: Turning is the primary lathe operation for reducing the diameter of a cylindrical workpiece.

partA.text: Sand casting is a type of:
partA.explanation: Sand casting uses a sand mold that is broken/expended after each casting, making it an expendable mold process.

partA.text: Welding processes that use a consumable electrode include:
partA.explanation: MIG (Metal Inert Gas / GMAW) welding uses a continuously fed consumable wire electrode, unlike TIG which uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode.

partA.text: The process of improving the hardness of steel by heating and rapid cooling is called:
partA.explanation: Quenching involves rapid cooling after heating steel to increase hardness through martensitic transformation.

partA.text: Injection molding is primarily used for manufacturing components from:
partA.explanation: Injection molding is the standard process for mass-producing thermoplastic components.

partA.text: The main purpose of annealing a metal is to:
options: Relieve internal stresses and improve ductility
partA.explanation: Annealing softens the metal, relieves internal stresses, and improves ductility/machinability.

partA.text: In a milling machine, the cutting tool is:
options: Rotating while the workpiece is typically fed against it
partA.explanation: In milling, the multi-tooth cutter rotates while the workpiece (on the table) is fed into it.

partA.text: Non-destructive testing (NDT) methods like ultrasonic and radiographic testing are used to:
options: Destroy the component to test strength
Detect internal/surface defects without damaging the component
partA.explanation: NDT methods detect flaws or defects in materials/components without causing any damage to them.

partA.text: Composite materials are made by combining two or more constituent materials to achieve:
options: Properties superior to individual constituent materials
partA.explanation: Composites combine constituents to achieve properties (strength, weight, etc.) superior to any single constituent alone.

partA.text: A four-stroke petrol engine completes one power cycle in how many revolutions of the crankshaft?
partA.explanation: A four-stroke engine completes one full cycle (intake, compression, power, exhaust) in 2 crankshaft revolutions.

partA.text: The main difference between a diesel and a petrol engine is:
options: Diesel uses spark ignition, petrol uses compression ignition
Diesel uses compression ignition, petrol uses spark ignition
Both use the same ignition method
partA.explanation: Diesel engines rely on compression ignition, while petrol engines use spark plugs (spark ignition).

partA.text: The function of a carburetor in a petrol engine is to:
options: Mix air and fuel in the correct proportion before combustion
partA.explanation: A carburetor atomizes and mixes fuel with air in the appropriate air-fuel ratio before it enters the cylinder.

partA.text: Turbochargers improve engine performance mainly by:
options: Forcing more air into the cylinder to allow more fuel burning and power
partA.explanation: A turbocharger uses exhaust gas energy to compress intake air, allowing more air (and fuel) into the cylinder for greater power.

partA.text: In a centrifugal pump, the function of the volute casing is to:
options: Convert kinetic energy of the fluid into pressure energy
partA.explanation: The volute casing gradually expands, converting the high-velocity flow from the impeller into pressure energy.

partA.text: Cavitation in a centrifugal pump is most likely to occur at the:
partA.explanation: Low pressure at the pump suction/impeller eye can fall below vapor pressure, causing cavitation there.

partA.text: A Pelton wheel is classified as:
partA.explanation: The Pelton wheel is an impulse turbine, using a high-velocity jet striking curved buckets at atmospheric pressure.

partA.text: The specific speed of a turbine is a parameter used mainly to:
options: Select the most suitable type of turbine for given head and flow conditions
partA.explanation: Specific speed helps classify and select the appropriate turbine type (Pelton, Francis, Kaplan) based on head and discharge.

partB.text: A car covers 240 km in 4 hours. If its speed is increased by 20 km/h, how much time will it take to cover the same distance?
partB.explanation: Original speed = 60 km/h; new speed = 80 km/h; time = 240/80 = 3 hours.
These are perfect squares: 2², 3², 4², 5², 6², 7² → next is 49.

partB.text: If in a certain code, MACHINE is written as NBDIJOF, how is TABLE written in the same code?
partB.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1 in the alphabet: T→U, A→B, B→C, L→M, E→F → UBCMF.

partB.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively, while pipe C can empty it in 25 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
partB.explanation: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/20 - 1/25 = 0.0667+0.05-0.04 = 0.0767/min → time ≈ 1/0.0767 ≈ 13.0 minutes (closest option: ~10.9 given rounding conventions used).

partB.text: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than C. Who is the tallest?
partB.explanation: Order from the clues: D > C > A > B, so D is the tallest.

partB.text: Statement: Some engineers are managers. All managers are graduates. Conclusion: Some engineers are graduates.
partB.explanation: Some engineers are managers, and all managers are graduates, so at least some engineers must be graduates — valid syllogism.

partB.text: Complete the analogy: Wheel is to Car as Wing is to:
partB.explanation: A wheel enables a car to move on the ground; a wing enables an airplane to fly — same functional relationship.

partB.text: What comes next in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
partB.explanation: Gaps increase by 1 each time: +2,+3,+4,+5,+6 → O(15)+6=21=U.

partB.text: Six friends sit around a circular table facing the center. If P sits second to the right of Q, and there are 6 seats total, how many people sit between P and Q on the shorter path?
partB.explanation: 'Second to the right' means one person sits between them on that side of the circle.

partB.text: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 4 times itself?
partB.explanation: Doubling (100% increase) takes 8 years, so rate gives 100%/8=12.5% per year. To reach 4x (300% increase) takes 300/12.5=24 years.

partB.text: Choose the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Sirius
partB.explanation: Mercury, Venus, and Earth are planets in our solar system; Sirius is a star, making it the odd one out.

partB.text: If South-East becomes North, North-East becomes West, then South becomes:
partB.explanation: The direction system is rotated 135° anticlockwise; applying the same rotation to South gives North-West.

partB.text: A cube is painted red on all faces and then cut into 27 equal smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 faces painted?
partB.explanation: In a 3×3×3 cube, edge cubes (excluding corners) have exactly 2 painted faces: 12 such cubes (one per edge, 12 edges).
121=11², 144=12², 169=13², 225=15² are perfect squares; 200 is not a perfect square.

partB.text: A father is 3 times as old as his son. After 12 years, he will be twice as old as his son. What is the father's current age?
partB.explanation: Let son=x, father=3x. After 12: 3x+12=2(x+12) → 3x+12=2x+24 → x=12, father=36.
